name: Sendinês (Mirandese meridional)
notes: Sendinês subdialect of Mirandese, spoken in Vila de Sendim (southern extreme of Terra de Miranda). It inherits the full Central Mirandese system (graphemes_base=mwl: apical ⟨s⟩ /s̺ z̺/ vs predorsal ⟨c,ç,z⟩ /s z/, ⟨x⟩ /ʃ/, ⟨j,g⟩ /ʒ/, ⟨ch⟩ /tʃ/, ⟨nh⟩ /ɲ/, nasal-vowel digraphs) and overrides only the two documented Sendinês deltas: (1) monophthongisation of the Leonese diphthongs ⟨iê/ie⟩ → /i/ and ⟨uô/uo⟩ → /u/ (tirra not tiêrra, curpo not cuôrpo) — the Central/Raiano [je]/[wo] is reduced to [i]/[u]; (2) DEPALATALISATION of /ʎ/ → /l/: words that other dialects say with ⟨lh⟩ /ʎ/ are said with /l/ (alá for alhá, lhado→lado, lhuç→[ˈlus], lhobo→[ˈlobu]), and word-initial ⟨l⟩ is likewise plain /l/ (no Leonese initial palatalisation). The Primeiro Aditamento à Convenção (February 2000) permits Sendinese writers to spell word-initial ⟨l-⟩ (not ⟨lh-⟩). Because ⟨lh⟩ → /l/ is overridden here, the Central word-initial ⟨l⟩ → /ʎ/ rule is also cancelled via the positional override (l stays /l/ in every position). The unstressed vowel qualities are inherited from Central Mirandese, where they are grounded in Leite de Vasconcelos's description of Duas-Igrejas (unstressed ⟨o u⟩ = [u], unstressed and final ⟨e⟩ = [ɨ]). Whether Sendinês realises those unstressed vowels differently is not settled by any description reached so far, and the Sendinês gold sample is too small to decide it; the inherited Central values stand until a published source says otherwise.

stress.notes: Convenção Ortográfica da Língua Mirandesa (1999) accentuation, Portuguese-based: paroxytone default; written accent (acute or tilde) overrides. Oxytone-attracting endings reflect Mirandese orthography: consonant-final r/l/z/ç (rapaç, Pertual, falar) and the final nasals written with -n in the Asturleonese manner — -in (camin, Sendin), -un, and the systematically oxytone -on class from Latin -ōnem (naçon, coraçon, Associaçon). Unmarked -an/-en verb endings stay paroxytone as in Portuguese -am/-em. Dialect mwl-x-sendim: no evidence of stress-pattern divergence from standard Mirandese; block copied from mwl (cliticless_words included, since stress is not inherited). Sendinês keeps the plain [l] for the article and depalatalises ⟨lh⟩/initial-⟨l⟩ to [l] by its own positional table, and monophthongises ⟨ie⟩→[i] so 'quien' → [ˈkĩ]; it therefore needs no word_exceptions overriding the mwl parent's.

mirandese_g2p.measured: The mirandese_g2p row holds 11 gold pairs, per=0.3258, per_ci_low=0.1641, per_ci_high=0.4824 (benchmarks/results.json). The 95% interval includes 0.25, so the row cannot be read as a failure. The parent mwl spec's own mirandese_g2p row draws on the same underlying source with 205 pairs and measures per=0.1317, well under the threshold; the 11-pair Sendim subset is too small to show whether it genuinely differs from that larger measurement or is simply noise (audit is OWN_ONLY and is not inherited from mwl).
